content:
olivia: Quick RFC follow-up — proposal to split the policy DSL into two clear layers: `intent` (fast, coarse runtime decisions) + `constraints` (expresses hard/soft limits). Heavy scoring/evals are moved to an async verifier that runs off-path and votes on decision quality.

raj: I like separating intent vs constraints. main question: what falls to runtime vs verifier? latency-sensitive routing must be <2ms. verifier can be seconds.

emily: The runtime needs an atomic token so it can admit requests immediately and later reconcile if verifier disagrees. without that we get race conditions when fallback triggers.

thomas: How do we handle verifier-detected mismatches? Do we force immediate rollback, or mark tenant and bias next N requests to fallback? need a safe, gradual remediation.

olivia: Sketch: runtime returns (decision, admission_token). verifier consumes traces and may emit one of: {OK, STALE_INFO, INVALID_CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION}. If INVALID -> increment a per-tenant "trust epoch" and add temporary penalty to route scorer for that epoch. penalty decays via TTL. All actions are auditable.

raj: Needs billing tie-in: verifier annotations should include observed cost delta so billing/optimize can re-label workloads. otherwise ops won't be able to reconcile unit economics.

emily: Also: versioned policies + seq numbers on decisions. verifier attaches policy_version it used. if verifier lags (policy_version < runtime_version) treat as STALE_INFO.

olivia: DSL example (very rough):

```
intent {
  goal: "prefer_low_latency"
  hedge: "allow_fallback_to_high_capacity"
}
constraints {
  max_cost_usd_per_1k: 0.5
  allowed_regions: ["us-east-1","eu-west-1"]
  hard: ["no-airgap-models"]
}
```

thomas: We should avoid creating explody combinatorics in constraints. runtime will only evaluate a tiny boolean subset. verifier runs the full scoring.

raj: Operational concerns: verifier needs resource isolation (dedicated pool) and strong sampling rules. we should not verifier-every-request. propose 1% sampling + targeted rechecks on anomalies.

emily: +1 to sampling. add triggers: unusual latency, cost delta, or model quality regression. verifier should also drive evals to adjust quantization suggestions.

infra-bot: deploy-check: canary policy-sync pipeline applied to staging at 1715305000 :white_check_mark:

olivia: Next steps: 1) write RFC with clear state machine for admission_token lifecycle, 2) define verifier output schema + score tags, 3) prototype token TTL/epoch logic in router. Volunteers?

raj: I can take the token lifecycle state machine.

emily: I'll draft verifier output schema and sampling policy.

thomas: I'll do a short runbook for remediation actions when verifier marks INVALID.

olivia: Great — I'll assemble RFC draft and ping infra for staging resources. Thanks! :rocket:
